name: Tim Yates
bio: Award-winning instrument builder, sound-artist and musician who makes, builds and finds instruments for performance and installation. Shown work at the Tate Modern, the V&A and Xi'an International Maker Faire. Runs the R&D programme at Drake Music and produces for Music Tech Fest.

name: Vulpestruments (Tom Fox)
bio: Tom Fox's project exploring reclaimed materials and odd bits of physics and technology to find new methods of sound creation and interaction. Shown at the Tate Modern, the V&A, the Royal College of Music and Art; runs workshops at UCA, LCC and Brighton University.

name: Gawain Hewitt
bio: Artist and composer known for combining technology with more traditional musical and artistic practices. Shown at Spitalfields Festival, the V&A and Tate Modern; part of the team that won the European Space Agency prize at Music Tech Fest 2018 for a satellite-data sonification piece.

name: Adrian Holder (Precis)
bio: Sound and visual artist who processes real-world sounds using anything from a hacked radio to MAX for Live, working across genres to convey the balance between audio and visual perception.

name: Jen Haugan
bio: Multidisciplinary designer with an MA in Information Experience Design from the RCA, creating tangible experiences with light and sound. Exhibited at Sónar+D and IRCAM. Runs design collective Studio Strohm.

name: Richard Grant (Son.im)
bio: Founder of Son.im, a studio bridging art and show-craft. Sculptural work combines acoustics with sight and smell to encourage audience participation. Has worked with NASA, Disney and Abbey Road Studios.

name: Ashleigh Fisk
bio: Multimedia artist working in ceramics, performance and sound, using archaeological and contemporary ceramics to summon historical characters through timeless sounds and folkloric narrative.

name: MyPandaShallFly (Suren Seneviratne)
bio: London-based producer whose remix work first got Pitchfork's attention in 2010. Has remixed The Weeknd and Little Boots, and played BBC Hackney Weekender, Outlook and Glade.

name: Andrew Hockey
bio: Composer and music technologist specialising in interactive instruments that let music be experienced outside a linear form. Featured on BBC Click, Berlin Maker Faire and the Old Truman Brewery.

name: Adam Paroussos (Bamboo Mustard)
bio: Sound designer, composer and performer who builds instruments and sound costumes for improvised audience performance. Runs multi-disciplinary event series Crossspace.

name: Brendan O'Connor
bio: Music technologist working on sound installations, compositions and audio applications. PhD student at Queen Mary University of London researching vocal behaviour with machine learning. Shown at Ars Electronica and We Are Robots.

name: Mother Disorder
bio: Performance piece Crystalline uses body-mounted microphones and foreboding electronic music, blending performance art and dark improvised sound around mental illness and neurodiversity.

name: Nick Murray
bio: London-based writer, composer and producer.

name: Amy Cutler
bio: Artist, cultural geographer, curator, writer and film-maker working with geography and nonhuman others. Has run live events with the BBC, Somerset House, Sheffield Doc/Fest, the Wellcome Trust, the Horniman Museum and Tate Modern. Performs as RAVINE/MACHINE with Scott Pitkethly.

name: Dom Aversano
bio: Multi-instrumentalist percussionist and composer whose primary instrument is the handpan, strongly influenced by konnakol, the Indian rhythmic vocal language.

name: Antosh Wojcik
bio: Poet, performer and Lecturer of Poetry and Creative Writing at the University of Winchester. One half of sound-art duo Post Everything.

name: Jenn Kirby
bio: Composer, performer, lecturer and music technologist. Programme Leader for MA Music at the University of the West of Scotland; founder of the Swansea Laptop Orchestra and Vice-President of the Irish Sound, Science and Technology Association.

name: Cutlasses (Scott Pitkethly)
bio: Solo project integrating the process of making music with the process of building the tools to make it — field recordings manipulated by DIY electronics, live guitar drones and cinematic melody. Also performs as RAVINE/MACHINE with Amy Cutler.

name: Gordon Charlton (Beat Frequency)
bio: Records and performs experimental theremin and computer-based music as Beat Frequency. Opened for thereminist Lydia Kavina at the 2010 Ether Festival, Royal Festival Hall.

name: Eastman Presser
bio: London-based musicker whose practice uses the interaction of sound and the body to playfully question how we listen and what counts as music — performed as Good Listener.

name: Bo Keeney
event: Hackoustic Village at We Are Robots
bio: Musician performing with a self-built, gesture-controlled instrument. Founded London Interactive Music Meetup (2015–17); released 13+ EPs and albums before moving into real-time responsive music research.

name: Kevin Ka Wei Chan (Gwaith Sŵn)
bio: London-based sound artist exploring memory, temporal location and political economy through redundant, discarded consumer audio technology. Collaborated with Tom Fox on the Proximity Mixer installation as part of collective Gwaith Sŵn. Exhibited at LCC, Universität der Künste Berlin and Science Gallery London.

name: Charles Matthews
bio: Sound artist and creative technologist working on augmented instruments and software for live performance and accessibility. Works with Drake Music and Hackoustic; teaches sonic arts at City Lit.

name: Diržytė (Gouda)
bio: Experimental music instrument designer, composer and sound artist working between the UK and Lithuania. Builds generative sound installations from self-built, electronics-augmented instrumentation, examining Eurocentrism in musical culture.

name: Ana Berkenhoff
bio: Versatile artist working across music, theatre, film, poetry, instrument building and installation. Regular UK/Germany performer, featured on Radio 3's Late Junction, BBC Introducing and Radiophrenia Glasgow.

name: Kuljit Bhamra
bio: Musician, performer and record producer; a pioneer of the British Bhangra sound and tabla player on Hollywood soundtracks. Runs Keda Music, developing tools to make Indian drumming more accessible.

name: Andrew McPherson
bio: Electrical engineer and composer who leads the Augmented Instruments Laboratory at Queen Mary University of London, and created Bela, an open-source platform for ultra-low-latency audio and sensor processing.

name: Stewart Easton
bio: Artist behind interactive tapestries that combine textile craft with sound and electronics.

name: Chloe Meineck
bio: Designer, maker, inventor and social entrepreneur based in Bristol and London. Founded Studio Meineck in 2016, working at the intersection of technology, craft and design — including Memory Boxes to support people with dementia.

name: Diego Baresch
bio: Post-doctoral researcher in Acoustics at Imperial College London, working on levitating and moving objects with sound waves, with a view to potential new cancer treatments.

name: Rodrigo Viterbo
bio: Portuguese Community Artist and Educator using music and making to work with people of all ages; runs workshops on didgeridoo-making from upcycled materials, including toilet rolls.

name: Look Mum No Computer
bio: Synth builder best known for the Synth Bike series of DIY modular instruments.

name: DADAMachines
bio: Berlin-based studio led by Johannes Lohbihler making music machines accessible to everyone. Their Automat toolkit Kickstarter hit 600% funding around the time of Hackoustic's showcase at Machines Room.

name: Tim Murray-Browne
bio: Artist and creative coder based in London working with code, sound, graphics and interactive technology, creating immersive spaces for installation and live performance that respond to the movement of the body.

name: Stephen Shiell
bio: Combines poetry, sonic art and hand-made instruments in installations and performances — including Ship's Opera, a live operatic concerto of ships' steam whistles, bells, horns and sirens on the VIC 96. Performs with Hannah White.

name: Laurel Smith-Pardue
bio: Performer working with an augmented violin.

name: Blanc Sceol
bio: Plays beautiful hand-made acoustic instruments.

name: Lula Mebrahtu
event: Daylight Music 339, EFG London Jazz Festival 2021
bio: Vocalist and early adopter of the MiMu interactive glove controller, using it to push the evolution of live music performance.

name: Jack Jelfs
bio: Sound artist behind Stop / Start, an ensemble of sculptural units generating sound to perform a musical composition on an endless, never-exactly-repeating loop. Shown at The Conservatoire, Blackheath.

name: Phlegmm
bio: Sound artist featured on The Hackompilation.

name: Harky
bio: Sound artist featured on The Hackompilation.

name: Kelly Snook
bio: Sound artist featured on The Hackompilation.

name: Frazer Merrick
bio: Sound artist featured on The Hackompilation and, later, the Hackoustic Orchestra line-up at Daylight Music 382.

name: Helen Leigh
bio: Maker of circuit-sculpture creatures — electronics-driven sculptural sound work.

name: Noum
bio: Sound artist featured on The Hackompilation.

name: #BarrysLounge
bio: Hackoustic's resident DJ, a fixture spinning discs at Hackoustic Presents nights since at least 2017.

name: Jacob Harrison
bio: PhD researcher in accessible instrument design; showed his one-handed bass guitar at Hackoustic Presents.

name: John Kelly
bio: Musician behind the Kellycaster, an accessible instrument developed with Drake Music and Gawain Hewitt.

name: Tasos Stamou
bio: Sound artist and instrument builder who showed work at Hackoustic's early London Hackspace sessions.

name: Optonoise (Stan Lewry)
bio: Builders of the Epsilonograph and Optomodule — experimental laser-beam instruments for generating sound and visuals, shown at Music Tech Fest Berlin and the new Tate Modern wing opening.

name: Blanca Regina & Matthias Kispert
bio: Ran the Material Studies workshop exploring the spontaneous sound within matter.

name: Craig Scott's Lobotomy
bio: Brings feedback mobiles and experimental sound installations to Hackoustic Presents nights.

name: Hannah Kemp-Welch
bio: Artist researching DIY antennas and radio receivers, showcased at Hackoustic's Iklectik night in October 2021.

name: Sarah Angliss
bio: Composer and roboticist working at the intersection of music, robotics and folklore, on the bill for Hackoustic's March 2023 Presents night.

name: Eevee Zayas
bio: Musician featured on the March 2023 Hackoustic Presents line-up.
